body.home.c1.1: In 2008 and 2009, Satoshi Nakamoto published [Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System (PDF)](https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf). The paper describes sending value online without a bank clearing the payment. Satoshi Nakamoto is the name on that paper.
body.home.c1.2: A blockchain is a shared ledger. Transactions are grouped into blocks. Each block is linked to the one before it by a hash. The network agrees on that chain of blocks.
body.home.c1.3: On Bitcoin, a buy or a sell is a transfer of unspent transaction outputs, called UTXOs. The transfer is broadcast. Miners can include it in a block. It is settled as more blocks are added after that one.
body.home.c1.5: [Read more: Bitcoin and the chain on Blind Bit Boys](/learn/bitcoin)
body.home.c2.6: In 2015, Ethereum added a general-purpose virtual machine. Programs on that machine are called smart contracts. Tokens are one thing those contracts can track.
body.home.c2.7: Tokens and smart contracts let a market run without one company operating the exchange. An automated market maker, or AMM, is a pool of tokens that prices a trade from a formula. Lending markets pool assets and charge borrowers. Stablecoins are tokens that aim to hold a steady value, often one dollar.
body.home.c2.8: DeFi is that layer: markets made of contracts instead of a single exchange operator. Fees and complexity are the honest downside. A crowded chain can cost a lot to use, and a contract does what it was written to do, including the mistakes.
body.home.c2.9: [Ethereum](https://ethereum.org/) publishes the network overview. [The Ethereum white paper](https://ethereum.org/whitepaper/) is the design document. The next chapter is the ladder of programs those contracts can be.
body.home.c2.10: [Read more: Ethereum and DeFi on Blind Bit Boys](/learn/ethereum)
body.home.c3.11: A smart contract is a program stored on a chain. You send a transaction, and the network runs that code the same way for everyone. No private server is the source of truth.
body.home.c3.12: Gas, the fee, pays validators to run the code. Bugs are public, and a mistake is often irreversible.
body.home.c3.13: The programs climb a ladder. A minimal token (ERC-20, or PRC-20 on PulseChain) stores a name, a symbol, balances, and transfer. A stablecoin, or a token in the HEX or PLS style, is still that balance contract plus extra rules. An NFT (ERC-721) uses unique ids, so one is not a substitute for another. A multisig or simple vault asks several keys to sign.
body.home.c3.14: An automated market maker holds two tokens and prices a trade with x times y equals k, the Uniswap v2 pattern. PulseX is that family on PulseChain. Lending contracts take collateral, charge interest, and liquidate if the price falls. Aave and Compound are Ethereum-style examples. Stablecoin issuer contracts mint and redeem against reserves or against other crypto. Bridges and intent routers lock, mint, or settle a swap across chains. Chapter 9 is that subject, including Liberty Swap. Staking and validator deposits are contracts too, on Ethereum and on PulseChain. Chapter 11 is where a node and a validator stake are described.
body.home.c3.15: [Read more: Smart contracts on Blind Bit Boys](/learn/smart-contracts)
body.home.c4.16: [Solana](https://solana.com/) is built for high throughput. Its runtime is different from the EVM, and the tradeoffs are different from Ethereum’s.
body.home.c4.17: [BNB Chain](https://www.bnbchain.org/), also called BNB Smart Chain, is an EVM-compatible chain associated with the Binance ecosystem. Fees are often lower than on Ethereum layer 1, and MetaMask-style wallets can use it for tokens, decentralized exchanges, and as a destination for bridges. It has its own validators and its own risks. It is not Binance the exchange. [BNB Chain docs](https://docs.bnbchain.org/) describe the network.
body.home.c4.18: Layer 2s on Ethereum post data to Ethereum and execute more cheaply off layer 1. Optimistic-style rollups include Arbitrum and Optimism. Base is an OP-stack chain. ZK-style examples include zkSync, Scroll, and Linea. [Ethereum’s layer 2 explainer](https://ethereum.org/en/layer-2/) is the official overview. To use one, the wallet needs that layer 2, you need a bridge or an official on-ramp, and a token can keep the same name while living in a different contract until it is bridged.
body.home.c4.19: [PulseChain](https://pulsechain.com/) is an Ethereum-style chain. It launched in May 2023, with cheaper fees and the coin PLS.
body.home.c4.21: [The official bridge](https://bridge.pulsechain.com/) moves assets from Ethereum.
body.home.c4.22: [scan.pulsechain.com](https://scan.pulsechain.com/) is where to scan PulseChain. PulseChain is home for the tools this site tests. Solana, BNB Chain, Ethereum, and the layer 2s above are networks in the same story.
body.home.c4.23: [Read more: Other blockchains, layer 2s, and PulseChain on Blind Bit Boys](/learn/chains)

That button sends you to partners, including Coinbase, Kraken, and Gemini. X is not a crypto exchange, and X does not custody those trades. [X](https://x.com/).

body.home.c6.31: A wallet here is software, or a hardware device, that holds keys and shows the addresses those keys control. This site will never ask you for a seed phrase. Who holds the keys, the company or you, is chapter 7.
body.home.c6.32: [Coinbase Wallet](https://wallet.coinbase.com/) is the self-custody wallet. It is separate from the Coinbase exchange. [MetaMask](https://metamask.io/) is another self-custody wallet.
body.home.c6.33: [Internet Money](https://internetmoney.io/) describes its wallet as non-custodial and open source, for Bitcoin, Ethereum, and EVM chains, and says it collects no data.
body.home.c6.34: ZKX Wallet comes from Liberty Swap. It is a self-custodial browser extension, and a web app that can be installed as a progressive web app (PWA). It supports PulseChain and other EVM chains. It includes Railgun public and private modes, and it can swap and bridge inside the wallet. Blind Bit Boys works with that team so ZKX can be used with JAWS or NVDA. That work is underway. This page does not claim the wallet is already perfect.
body.home.c6.35: [What is ZKX Wallet](https://docs.libertyswap.finance/zkx-wallet/what-is-zkx-wallet) is the Liberty Swap page for that product.
body.home.c6.36: The extension is listed as [ZKX Web3 Wallet on the Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/zkx-web3-wallet/fibfaangghabdbndamiaceoahiajfgck), offered by LibertySwap Developer.
body.home.c6.37: [Read more: Wallets on Blind Bit Boys](/learn/wallets)
body.home.c7.38: On a custodial exchange, the company holds the coins. You have a login. They run the keys. They can freeze a withdrawal. You are trusting their security and their solvency.
body.home.c7.39: A self-custody wallet is software or hardware that holds the keys on your side. The chain only sees an address. The wallets in chapter 6 are that kind of tool.
body.home.c7.40: An address, derived from a public key, is safe to share so someone can pay you. A private key or a seed phrase proves control. Anyone who has it can empty the wallet. Never type it into a website, a Discord message, or a “support chat.”
body.home.c7.41: “Not your keys, not your coins” means that if you do not control the private key, you have an IOU at that company. When a custodian is hacked, insolvent, or blocks withdrawals, users can lose access. In February 2014, Mt. Gox halted withdrawals and closed the exchange. On 28 February 2014 it filed for bankruptcy protection in Japan. On 10 November 2022, FTX suspended withdrawals. On 11 November 2022 it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States. Hot-wallet thefts at various centralized venues are the same kind of history. The lesson is counterparty risk.
body.home.c7.42: Self-custody has its own risks: a phishing site or a fake extension, a lost seed with no backup, malware that swaps the address on your clipboard, and a send on the wrong chain. Use the wallet hosts on [Official Links](/official-links). Write the seed on paper, offline. A hardware wallet from that vendor’s own site is optional. Send a small test first. Read the address back. Keep the software updated. Blind Bit Boys does not store user keys. This is education, not advice.
body.home.c7.43: [Read more: Who holds the keys on Blind Bit Boys](/learn/custody)

body.home.c9.57: A bridge locks or burns assets on one chain and mints or releases a representation on another. The risks are a wrong site and contract bugs. The token you receive can be a claim on the original, not the original coin itself.
body.home.c9.58: The [official PulseChain bridge](https://bridge.pulsechain.com/) moves value between Ethereum and PulseChain.
body.home.c9.59: [Liberty Swap](https://libertyswap.finance/) describes in-wallet swap and bridge through ZKX.
body.home.c9.60: Its [docs](https://docs.libertyswap.finance/) describe that published product. It is not a promise of every chain, and it is not a promise that every route is free.

body.home.c10.62: Providing liquidity means depositing a pair of tokens into an automated-market-maker pool, the Uniswap-style pool that runs on EVM chains. You receive a share of the trading fees. A farm pays an extra token on top of that deposit. Solana has farms where a protocol offers them. A payment can fail to arrive.
body.home.c10.63: Impermanent loss is the gap between holding the tokens in the pool and simply holding them in a wallet. Contract bugs can drain a pool. A fake site can imitate the real exchange.
body.home.c10.64: At this point Blind Bit Boys finds PulseChain the most practical chain for screen-reader DeFi, using [PulseX](https://app.pulsex.com/). [Liberty Swap Finance](https://libertyswap.finance/) is the other part of that path. That is a judgment about this project’s work. [Uniswap docs](https://docs.uniswap.org/) explain the pool pattern those EVM exchanges share.

body.home.c11.66: With some programming and systems skill, you can run your own node. Pruned mode saves disk. An archive of everything is huge. People run one on their own hardware, often with Docker and a compose file, or on a rented server. A hosted “node as a service” can give you an RPC. That is not the same as validating.
body.home.c11.68: Ethereum needs an execution client and a consensus client. [Ethereum nodes and clients](https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/nodes-and-clients/) is the overview.
body.home.c11.69: BNB Chain publishes its steps in the [BNB Chain docs](https://docs.bnbchain.org/).
body.home.c11.70: Solana validator and RPC notes are in the [Solana docs](https://solana.com/docs).
body.home.c11.71: PulseChain uses go-pulse plus Lighthouse or Prysm clients forked for the chain. Start at [pulsechain.com](https://pulsechain.com/). That site says running a single node requires a deposit of 32,000,000 PLS.
body.home.c11.72: That page links the [PulseChain Launchpad](https://launchpad.pulsechain.com/) for how to run a node.
body.home.c11.74: Confirm the 32,000,000 PLS deposit on pulsechain.com before sending funds. Gas is extra. Running a validator is optional and operationally heavy. Blind Bit Boys is working with a few teams so non-programmers can get a node up with clearer, accessible steps. This page does not name an unreleased product, and it does not promise an easy fortune.

body.home.c12.76: A block explorer is a search engine for one chain. You look up an address, a transaction hash, a token, or a block. The page shows sender, receiver, amount, fee, and status. It reads public data, often from a node. It does not move funds.
body.home.c12.77: Behind the page is an indexer and a site, sitting on RPC or node data. Two explorers can read the same chain and still disagree on labels. The chain is the record. Check that you are on the real domain before you paste an address.
body.home.c12.78: Those fields are text. JAWS or NVDA can read them when the explorer page exposes that text. This page does not certify those sites.
body.home.c12.81: PulseChain: [scan.pulsechain.com](https://scan.pulsechain.com/) and [ipfs.scan.pulsechain.com](https://ipfs.scan.pulsechain.com/). pulsechain.com lists that second host as its block explorer URL.
body.home.c12.88: mempool.space did not open when this page was checked, so it is not linked. pulsechain.com and scan.pulsechain.com do not link an Otterscan host, so this page does not add one. What that public record means for privacy is chapter 13.

body.home.c13.90: Most popular chains are transparent. Anyone with a block explorer can follow an address. “Pseudonymous” means the chain shows an address, not a legal name. It does not mean the activity is private.
body.home.c13.91: On Bitcoin, Ethereum, PulseChain, BNB Chain, and Solana, a normal transfer is public. Sender, receiver, and amount can be read by anyone who looks.
body.home.c13.92: Mixers and shady “privacy apps” carry high legal risk and high scam risk. This page does not recommend them, does not describe how to use them, and does not suggest breaking the law.
body.home.c13.93: [Railgun](https://railgun.org/) is a privacy system for EVM-style chains. Users can shield a balance into a private pool, transfer inside that pool, and later unshield back to a public address. That is the shape of the system. This page does not walk the steps.
body.home.c13.94: ZKX Wallet, from Liberty Swap, integrates Railgun so Public Mode and Private Mode live in the same self-custodial wallet. The product page is [What is ZKX Wallet](https://docs.libertyswap.finance/zkx-wallet/what-is-zkx-wallet). Blind Bit Boys works with that team on accessibility of those modes for people who use JAWS or NVDA. That work is underway. Private mode is not a claim that every observer is blind to the activity, and it is not a claim that the mode is legal in every country. Users have to follow the law where they live.

body.home.c14.97: The GENIUS Act is US law for payment stablecoins. It was signed on 18 July 2025. The rules are still rolling in. They were not finished at the one-year mark, and the statute’s fallback timing runs toward 18 January 2027. It does not legalize all crypto. [GENIUS Act bill text on Congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1582/text).
body.home.c14.98: The CLARITY Act passed the House in July 2025. Senate cloture failed on 15 September 2026. It is not law.
body.home.c14.99: The public actors here are Congress, the Treasury, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). The European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation, MiCA, is the large regime outside the United States.

body.learn.bitcoin.129: In 2008 and 2009, Satoshi Nakamoto published a paper for sending value online without a bank clearing the payment. Satoshi Nakamoto is the name on that paper.
body.learn.bitcoin.131: A blockchain is a shared ledger. Transactions are grouped into blocks. Each block is linked to the one before it by a hash, a short fingerprint of the earlier block. If someone changes an old block, the fingerprints no longer match, and the rest of the network can see the break.
body.learn.bitcoin.132: No single company keeps the only copy. Many computers hold the ledger, and the network agrees on which chain of blocks is the record.
body.learn.bitcoin.133: Buys and sells are UTXO transfers
body.learn.bitcoin.134: On Bitcoin, a coin you can spend is an unspent transaction output, called a UTXO. A payment points at outputs you already received and creates new outputs for the next owners. The transfer is broadcast to the network. Miners can put it in a block. It is settled as more blocks are built on top of that one. More confirmations mean more work would have to be redone to change that payment.
body.learn.bitcoin.136: [Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System (PDF)](https://bitcoin.org/bitcoin.pdf) is the white paper. [Bitcoin.org](https://bitcoin.org/) is the project site. Running the software yourself is covered in [Running your own node](/learn/nodes).
body.learn.bridges.137: A bridge locks or burns assets on one chain and mints or releases a representation on another. The asset you receive can be a claim on the original, not the original coin itself. That claim is only as good as the bridge contracts and the people or proofs behind them.
body.learn.bridges.139: Contract bugs can mint extra claims or trap the locked assets. A wrong or fake interface can send the transaction to a copy of the bridge. Wrapping means the token on the destination chain is a different contract from the token you started with, even when the ticker looks the same.
body.learn.bridges.141: The [official PulseChain bridge](https://bridge.pulsechain.com/) moves value between Ethereum and PulseChain. Other ecosystems publish their own official bridges. A bridge from a random site that uses the PulseChain name is not this one. Chapter 4 explains why a layer 2 bridge is a different hop from this Ethereum-to-PulseChain bridge. Chapter 8 is the list of swap venues that stay on their own chains.
body.learn.bridges.143: Liberty Swap describes its product as intent-based swapping and bridging. The [docs](https://docs.libertyswap.finance/) and [the site](https://libertyswap.finance/) advertise a zero-fee PulseChain decentralized exchange, and in-wallet swap and bridge through ZKX. When that flow is turned on, you move among the chains they support from ZKX, without a separate website. That is their published product. It is not a promise that every chain is included, and it is not a promise of zero fees on every route.
body.learn.buy-crypto.144: A centralized venue is a company that holds customer accounts and matches or fills orders on its own books. The coins you buy there sit in that account until you withdraw them. That is different from a wallet you control, which is chapter 6. Chapter 7 is who holds the keys.
body.learn.buy-crypto.146: [Kraken](https://www.kraken.com/), [Coinbase](https://www.coinbase.com/), and [Robinhood](https://robinhood.com/) are centralized exchanges. The usual path is to create an account, complete identity checks (often called KYC), buy bitcoin, ether, or another asset they list, and withdraw to a wallet you control when you are ready. Until that withdrawal confirms, the company can freeze, limit, or delay the account under its own rules and the rules it answers to.
body.learn.buy-crypto.148: [Cash App](https://cash.app/) offers Bitcoin for many US users. It does not follow that every US resident can use it.
body.learn.buy-crypto.150: On X, as of September 2026, X Money is a fiat payments product, in beta for premium users in the United States. A cashtag such as $BTC can show a chart and a Trade button. That button sends you to partners, including Coinbase, Kraken, and Gemini. X is not a crypto exchange, and X does not custody those trades. Buying from the Trade button means buying at the partner, under that partner’s account rules. [X](https://x.com/).
body.learn.chains.151: Bitcoin and Ethereum are not the only ledgers. Each network below settles its own record, or, in the case of a layer 2, posts that record back to Ethereum. PulseChain is where the tools on this site are tested. It is one chain on this list.

body.learn.chains.160: Not the EVM. The script system is for payments.
body.learn.chains.161: A market fee per transaction. It rises when blocks are full.
body.learn.chains.165: Yes. This is the EVM other chains copy.

body.learn.chains.174: Its own validators. Associated with the Binance ecosystem. It is not Binance the exchange.

body.learn.chains.180: The ones named on the story are EVM rollups. You still add that network in the wallet.

body.learn.chains.184: Its own validators. An Ethereum-style chain that launched in May 2023.

body.learn.chains.190: An own layer 1 settles on its own validators or miners. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, BNB Chain, and PulseChain are each their own layer 1. A bridge between them moves a representation of an asset. It does not merge their security. BNB Chain has its own validator set and its own risks. Holding an account at Binance the company is a different fact from holding a token on BNB Chain.
body.learn.chains.192: A rollup executes transactions away from Ethereum layer 1 and posts the data, or a proof, back to Ethereum. Users pay less because the heavy work is batched. Optimistic-style rollups include Arbitrum and Optimism. Base is an OP-stack chain in that family. ZK-style examples include zkSync, Scroll, and Linea. They use proofs instead of a waiting period, and the designs differ.
body.learn.chains.193: To use one, the wallet needs that layer 2 added as a network. You arrive with a bridge or an official on-ramp. A token can keep a familiar name and still be a different contract until it is bridged. The balance on Arbitrum is not the same contract entry as the balance on Ethereum layer 1.
body.learn.chains.195: A sidechain is its own chain, with its own validators, connected to another chain by a bridge. It is not a rollup: Ethereum does not settle the sidechain’s blocks. If the sidechain’s validators fail, the bridge does not inherit Ethereum’s security by itself. PulseChain is not an Ethereum layer 2. It is its own layer 1 that speaks the EVM and links to Ethereum through a bridge.
body.learn.chains.197: PulseChain launched in May 2023. Fees are cheaper than on Ethereum layer 1. The coin is PLS. [PulseX](https://pulsex.com/) is the main decentralized exchange. [The official bridge](https://bridge.pulsechain.com/) moves assets between Ethereum and PulseChain. [scan.pulsechain.com](https://scan.pulsechain.com/) describes itself as where to scan PulseChain. It shows blocks and transactions the network has accepted. The scanner is still a website in front of a node. [Running your own node](/learn/nodes) is how you check that record yourself.
body.learn.custody.198: Chapter 6 names wallet software. This chapter is who holds the keys behind a balance. It is education, not advice. Blind Bit Boys does not store user keys, and this site will never ask you for a seed phrase.
body.learn.custody.200: On a custodial exchange, the company holds the coins. You have a login. They run the keys. A withdrawal is a request they can approve, delay, or freeze under their rules and the rules they answer to. You are trusting their security and their solvency. Until a withdrawal confirms on the chain you chose, the balance is an entry on that company’s books.
body.learn.custody.201: Kraken, Coinbase, Robinhood, and Cash App, in chapter 5, are examples of companies in that role. X is not. A cashtag Trade button sends you to a partner. The partner still holds the coins until you withdraw.
body.learn.custody.203: A self-custody wallet is software or hardware that holds the keys on your side. The chain only sees an address. Coinbase Wallet, MetaMask, Internet Money, and ZKX, in [chapter 6](/learn/wallets), are that kind of tool. They are not the exchange that shares a brand name. Assets in a Coinbase exchange account are not the same record as assets in Coinbase Wallet until you withdraw.
body.learn.custody.205: An address is derived from a public key. It is safe to share so someone can pay you. Publishing an address also lets anyone read that address on an explorer. That is public data, not a secret you can take back.
body.learn.custody.206: A private key, or the seed phrase that can recreate it, proves control. Anyone who has it can empty the wallet. Never type it into a website, a Discord message, or a “support chat.” A real wallet vendor does not need the seed to help you install the software. Blind Bit Boys will not ask for it.
body.learn.custody.207: Not your keys, not your coins
body.learn.custody.208: “Not your keys, not your coins” means that if you do not control the private key, you have an IOU at that company. The company can be honest and still fail. The IOU is only as good as their books, their security, and their ability to pay withdrawals.
body.learn.custody.210: When a custodian is hacked, insolvent, or blocks withdrawals, users can lose access. This is history, not a how-to. In February 2014, Mt. Gox halted withdrawals and closed the exchange. On 28 February 2014 it filed for bankruptcy protection in Japan. On 10 November 2022, FTX suspended withdrawals. On 11 November 2022 it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States. Hot-wallet thefts at various centralized venues are the same kind of history: coins the company was holding became coins the users could not withdraw. The lesson is counterparty risk. This page does not give dollar figures and does not describe how those failures were carried out.
body.learn.custody.212: Self-custody moves the risks onto the key holder.
body.learn.custody.213: A phishing site or a fake extension copies a wallet’s name and asks you to type a seed or sign a broad approval.
body.learn.custody.214: A lost seed with no backup is final. The company cannot reset a key it never held.
body.learn.custody.215: Malware can swap the address on your clipboard, so the address you paste is not the one you copied.
body.learn.custody.216: A send on the wrong chain does not arrive as the same balance. The same address text can exist on more than one EVM chain, and the coins still live on the chain you actually used.
body.learn.custody.218: Use the wallet hosts on [Official Links](/official-links). Type the address yourself or use a bookmark you already trust. Write the seed on paper, offline, and store that paper where a website cannot see it. A hardware wallet from that vendor’s own site is optional. Send a small test first. Read the full address on the device you are sending from, not only the first and last characters. Keep the wallet software updated. None of that is a promise against loss. It is the ordinary care this page can describe. It is education, not advice.
body.learn.dex.219: A centralized exchange holds the coins in its account. A decentralized exchange swaps inside a wallet. The swap is a call to a smart contract. The coins move from your address to the pool, and the pool sends the other token back, if the transaction succeeds.
body.learn.dex.220: The wallet has to be on the right network
body.learn.dex.221: A PulseX pool does not see an Ethereum balance. A Uniswap pool does not see a BNB Chain balance. Before you approve anything, the wallet’s network must be the chain where that pool lives. Adding the network is a setting in the wallet. The same address can exist on several chains, and the balances are still separate.
body.learn.dex.223: Approve. You send a transaction that lets the exchange contract move up to a set amount of the token you are selling. Approval is its own transaction and its own fee. It does not yet swap.
body.learn.dex.224: Swap. You send a second transaction. The contract takes the sold token and sends the bought token according to the pool’s price, minus the pool’s fee. If you set a minimum you will accept and the price has moved past it, the swap can revert. You still paid the fee for the attempt.
body.learn.dex.226: An automated market maker, or AMM, is a pool of two tokens. The Uniswap v2 pattern prices a trade from the two reserves. PulseX, PancakeSwap, QuickSwap, Raydium, and Sushi are in this family, each on the chains they actually deploy.
body.learn.dex.227: An aggregator does not have to be the pool. Jupiter, on Solana, searches other venues and builds a route. You still sign in your wallet. The route can touch more than one program. Read the route before you confirm it.
body.learn.dex.229: Bookmark these. A search ad and a similar name are how fake swap sites spread.
body.learn.dex.237: On Avalanche, [Trader Joe](https://traderjoexyz.com/) is the familiar venue. That address currently redirects to lfj.gg.
body.learn.dex.239: A lookalike uses a close name, a copied logo, and a page that asks you to approve a contract. That approval can let the contract move your tokens. This site will never ask for a seed phrase. Type the host yourself, or use a bookmark you created from the links above. Do not trust a domain that is one letter off, or a “PulseX” site that is not pulsex.com or app.pulsex.com.
body.learn.dex.241: PulseX and [Liberty Swap](https://libertyswap.finance/) are this project’s accessible swap path. The other venues on this page are real exchanges. They are listed so you can tell an official host from a copy. This page does not claim they are certified for JAWS or NVDA.
body.learn.ethereum.242: In 2015, Ethereum added a general-purpose virtual machine. Bitcoin’s ledger mostly records payments. Ethereum’s ledger can also store programs and run them when someone sends a transaction.
body.learn.ethereum.244: Those programs are smart contracts. Tokens are one thing a contract can track. The network, not a private server, is the source of truth for what the code did. [Smart contracts](/learn/smart-contracts) walks the ladder from a plain token to exchanges, loans, and bridges.
body.learn.ethereum.246: Tokens and smart contracts let a market run without one company operating the exchange. An automated market maker, or AMM, is a pool of tokens that prices a trade from a formula. Lending markets pool assets and charge borrowers. Stablecoins are tokens that aim to hold a steady value, often one dollar.
body.learn.ethereum.247: DeFi is that layer: markets made of contracts instead of a single exchange operator. Fees and complexity are the honest downside. A crowded chain can cost a lot to use, and a contract does what it was written to do, including the mistakes.
body.learn.ethereum.249: [Ethereum](https://ethereum.org/) publishes the network overview. [The Ethereum white paper](https://ethereum.org/whitepaper/) is the design document.
body.learn.explorers.250: A block explorer is a search engine for one chain. You look up an address, a transaction hash, a token, or a block. It reads public data, often from a node or from an indexer in front of that node. It does not move funds, and it does not hold your keys.
body.learn.explorers.252: A transaction page shows the sender, the receiver, the amount, the fee, and a status such as success or failure. A block page shows the transactions that landed together. Two explorers can read the same chain and still disagree on a token’s name or a label. The chain is the record. The site is a view of it.
body.learn.explorers.253: Those fields are text. JAWS or NVDA can read them when the explorer page exposes that text. This page does not certify those sites for any screen reader.
body.learn.explorers.255: Check the domain before you paste. Use a host from the list below or from [Official Links](/official-links). Copy the address from your wallet. Paste it into the explorer’s search. Read the page that opens. Paste an address or a transaction hash. Do not paste a seed phrase. The explorer does not need one, and a box that asks for one is not an explorer.
body.learn.explorers.257: After you paste a transaction hash, read these fields in order:
body.learn.explorers.258: Status. Success means the chain accepted it. Failure means it did not, and the fee can still be gone.
body.learn.explorers.259: From. The address that signed the transaction.
body.learn.explorers.260: To. The address or the contract that received it.
body.learn.explorers.261: Amount. What moved, and which token. A token transfer can sit inside a contract call.
body.learn.explorers.262: Fee. What the sender paid the network. The explorer did not collect that fee.
body.learn.explorers.263: Block. The block that contains the transaction, once it is included.
body.learn.explorers.265: A token page can include a holders tab. That list is public. Anyone can see addresses that hold the token and, on many explorers, how much. Looking yourself up does not make the holding private. Do not treat a holder list as a secret, and do not assume a label on an address is the person’s legal name.
body.learn.explorers.267: mempool.space did not open when this page was checked, so it is not linked. pulsechain.com and scan.pulsechain.com do not link an Otterscan host, so this page does not guess one. pulsechain.com lists ipfs.scan.pulsechain.com as its block explorer URL.
body.learn.explorers.277: The same hosts are grouped on [Official Links](/official-links). What a public explorer means for privacy is [chapter 13](/learn/privacy).
body.learn.nodes.278: With some programming and systems skill, you can run your own node. A node checks the chain on a machine you operate. A website such as [scan.pulsechain.com](https://scan.pulsechain.com/) can show the same blocks. The website is still someone else’s server until you verify it.
body.learn.nodes.279: Blind Bit Boys is working with a few teams so non-programmers can get a node up with clearer, accessible steps. This page does not name an unreleased product.
body.learn.nodes.281: Your own hardware. The computer stays in a place you control. Power, disk, and an open port are your problem. Docker and a compose file are a common way to start the clients together.
body.learn.nodes.282: A virtual private server. You rent a machine in a data center and install the same software. You still operate the node. The host operates the hardware.
body.learn.nodes.283: A hosted “node as a service,” when you only need an RPC: a remote server that answers chain questions. That is not validating. You are trusting the operator’s answer unless you also run a node that checks it.
body.learn.nodes.285: Bitcoin Core can run pruned or full. Pruned mode saves disk after the state is checked. An archive of every historical state is much larger. [Bitcoin Core](https://bitcoin.org/en/bitcoin-core/).
body.learn.nodes.287: Ethereum needs an execution client and a consensus client. People run full, snap, or archive modes. Snap sync reaches the current state faster. Archive is huge. [Ethereum nodes and clients](https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/nodes-and-clients/).
body.learn.nodes.289: [BNB Chain docs](https://docs.bnbchain.org/) publish how to run a node for that chain. A BNB Chain node does not check Ethereum or PulseChain.
body.learn.nodes.291: Solana’s current documentation for validators and RPC is at [solana.com/docs](https://solana.com/docs). Follow that path rather than an old mirror. A Solana validator is a different client from an EVM execution client.
body.learn.nodes.293: Start at [pulsechain.com](https://pulsechain.com/). That site says running a single node requires a deposit of 32,000,000 PLS. Operators use go-pulse, plus Lighthouse or Prysm clients forked for PulseChain.
body.learn.nodes.294: Details on that site point to the [PulseChain Launchpad](https://launchpad.pulsechain.com/).
body.learn.nodes.295: They also point to the [PulseChain mainnet node notes](https://gitlab.com/pulsechaincom/pulsechain-mainnet#advanced-users-running-a-pulsechain-node).
body.learn.nodes.296: Confirm the 32,000,000 PLS deposit on pulsechain.com before sending funds. Gas is extra. Validators can receive rewards and can be slashed. Running one is optional and operationally heavy. It is not a shortcut to profit.
body.learn.policy.297: As of 24 September 2026, the United States is building market-structure rules for crypto. Those rules are not finished. This page is a description of public statutes and regulators. It is not legal advice, and it is not investment advice.
body.learn.policy.299: The GENIUS Act is US law. It was signed on 18 July 2025. The statute’s name is the Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins Act. It is a federal framework for payment stablecoins. Implementing rules were not finished by the one-year mark. The statute’s fallback timing runs toward 18 January 2027.
body.learn.policy.300: The GENIUS Act does not legalize all crypto. It does not turn every token into a payment stablecoin, and it does not finish the market-structure questions below. [GENIUS Act bill text on Congress.gov](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/senate-bill/1582/text).
body.learn.policy.302: The CLARITY Act, the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act, passed the House in July 2025. Senate cloture failed on 15 September 2026. It is not enacted. It is not current law.
body.learn.policy.303: Who writes and enforces the rules
body.learn.policy.304: The public actors in this chapter are Congress, the Treasury, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC). Congress writes statutes. Treasury and the market regulators write and enforce rules inside the authority those statutes give them.
body.learn.policy.306: The European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation, MiCA, is the large existing regime outside this US story. Many countries license exchanges. This page does not invent a list of those countries.
body.learn.policy.308: Centralized exchanges still use identity checks, often called KYC, where their regulators require it. Self-custody means you hold the keys. It is not a license to ignore the law where you live. Tax, sanctions, and securities rules can still apply to a transaction you sign yourself.
body.learn.privacy.309: Most popular chains are transparent. Anyone with a block explorer can follow an address. “Pseudonymous” means the chain shows an address, not a legal name. It does not mean the activity is private. Chapter 12 is how to read that public record.
body.learn.privacy.311: An address can be used without printing a legal name on the chain. The transfers are still a public list. If an address is tied to an exchange account, a public post, or a payment someone knows about, the rest of that address’s history can be read by anyone with an explorer.
body.learn.privacy.313: On Bitcoin, Ethereum, PulseChain, BNB Chain, and Solana, a normal transfer is public. Sender, receiver, and amount can be read by anyone who looks. A new address is not a privacy system. It is another public address.
body.learn.privacy.315: Mixers and shady “privacy apps” carry high legal risk and high scam risk. This page does not recommend them. It does not describe how to use them. It does not suggest hiding proceeds or breaking the law. A site that asks for a seed phrase and promises privacy is a theft, not a tool.
body.learn.privacy.317: [Railgun](https://railgun.org/) is a privacy system for EVM-style chains. At a high level, users can shield a balance into a private pool, transfer inside that pool, and later unshield back to a public address. Shielded activity is the point of the pool. Unshielding returns value to a public address, which an explorer can see again. This page does not walk those steps, and it does not claim the pool hides a person from every observer.
body.learn.privacy.319: ZKX Wallet, from Liberty Swap, integrates Railgun so Public Mode and Private Mode live in the same self-custodial wallet. The wallet itself is [chapter 6](/learn/wallets). The product page is [What is ZKX Wallet](https://docs.libertyswap.finance/zkx-wallet/what-is-zkx-wallet).
body.learn.privacy.320: Blind Bit Boys works with that team on accessibility of those modes for people who use JAWS or NVDA. That work is underway. This page does not claim the wallet is already perfect. Private mode is not a claim that every observer is blind to the activity, and it is not a claim that the mode is legal in every country. Users have to follow the law where they live.
body.learn.privacy.321: The same links are on [Official Links](/official-links). This page is education, not advice, and not a promise about what any investigator, exchange, or court can see.
body.learn.smart-contracts.322: A smart contract is a program stored on a chain. A person sends a transaction. Every node that follows the rules runs that code the same way. No private server is the source of truth. Gas, the fee, pays validators to run the code. Bugs are public, and a mistake is often irreversible.
body.learn.smart-contracts.323: [Ethereum’s smart contract guide](https://ethereum.org/en/smart-contracts/) is the plain-language overview. The rungs below go from a balance sheet to a bridge.
body.learn.smart-contracts.325: A minimal token contract stores a name, a symbol, and a balance for each address. Transfer moves a balance from one address to another. ERC-20 is the common Ethereum pattern. [The ERC-20 standard](https://ethereum.org/en/developers/docs/standards/tokens/erc-20/) describes it. PRC-20 is the same idea on PulseChain. A stablecoin, or a token in the HEX or PLS style, is still that balance contract plus extra rules. The extra rules do not make the balance magic.
body.learn.smart-contracts.327: An ERC-721 contract tracks unique ids. Token number 10 is not a substitute for token number 11, even when the collection shares a name. You transfer an id, not a pile of interchangeable units.
body.learn.smart-contracts.329: A simple vault holds assets and pays them out only when enough keys sign. A two-of-three vault needs two of the three holders. One lost key does not have to empty the vault. One stolen key does not have to either, if the threshold is higher than one.
body.learn.smart-contracts.331: An automated market maker holds a pool of two tokens. The Uniswap v2 pattern prices a trade from x times y equals k: the two reserves, multiplied, stay near a constant. A larger trade moves the price more. PulseX is this family on PulseChain. [The PulseX app](https://app.pulsex.com/) is one place that pool is used.
body.learn.smart-contracts.333: A lending contract lets someone deposit one asset and borrow another. Aave and Compound are Ethereum-style examples. [Aave](https://aave.com/) is one of those projects. This page does not claim either system is safe.
body.learn.smart-contracts.334: Collateral is the asset you lock so the protocol can sell it if the loan is no longer covered. It is the lender’s security, not a gift.
body.learn.smart-contracts.335: Interest is the payment borrowers make for the time they hold the loan. People who supplied the pool may receive a share. The rate can change with demand, and a displayed rate is not a promise.
body.learn.smart-contracts.336: Liquidation is the sale of collateral when its price falls too far, or when the debt grows past the protocol’s limit. The borrower can lose the locked asset. A fast price move can trigger that sale before a person reacts.
body.learn.smart-contracts.338: A stablecoin issuer contract mints a token that aims to stay near a set value, often one dollar, and redeems it under its own rules. A USDC-style issuer mints against off-chain reserves such as cash and short-term government debt, and a company stands behind the redeem window. A DAI-style issuer mints against crypto locked in contracts, and liquidation protects the peg when collateral prices fall. Both are still contracts plus the rules around them. Neither sentence is a claim that the peg will hold.
body.learn.smart-contracts.340: Some contracts lock or burn an asset on one chain and mint or release a representation on another. An intent router takes a signed request (“I want this asset on that chain”) and settles it if the terms match. Chapter 9 is that subject, including the official PulseChain bridge and what [Liberty Swap](https://libertyswap.finance/) publishes about swaps and bridges.
body.learn.smart-contracts.342: Ethereum and PulseChain use deposit contracts so a validator can lock the stake the protocol requires. The contract records the deposit. It does not run the validator’s computers. Rewards and slashing live in the protocol rules. Chapter 10 covers liquidity and farms. Chapter 11 covers running a node and the PulseChain validator role.
body.learn.smart-contracts.343: A swap, one step at a time
body.learn.smart-contracts.344: This is the shape of a typical pool swap. It is not a button-by-button guide for one website.
body.learn.smart-contracts.345: Approve. You send a transaction that lets the exchange contract move up to a set amount of token A from your address. Approval is its own transaction, with its own fee. It does not yet move the tokens.
body.learn.smart-contracts.346: Swap. You send a second transaction that calls the pool. The contract takes token A and sends token B according to the pool’s formula, minus the fee the pool charges. You can usually set a minimum amount of token B you will accept. If the price has moved past that minimum, the transaction reverts and you keep token A, but you still paid the fee for the attempt.
body.learn.smart-contracts.347: New balances. Your address holds less A and more B. The pool holds more A and less B. Anyone can read those balances on the chain after the block is accepted.
body.learn.smart-contracts.349: A rug is a drain that the code allows. If the deployer can pull the pool, mint unlimited tokens, or redirect fees, the contract can be emptied while it still “works as written.”
body.learn.smart-contracts.350: Upgrade keys mean an admin can replace the code later. A contract that looked limited on Monday can follow new rules on Friday. A frozen contract has no such key. Many popular contracts do.
body.learn.smart-contracts.351: Oracle failure means a price feed the contract trusts is wrong, late, or captured. Lending markets and some stablecoins liquidate or mint from that price. A bad price can sell collateral that a calm market would have left alone.
body.learn.smart-contracts.352: Phishing sites copy a name and a logo and ask you to sign. The signature can grant a contract permission to move your tokens. Blind Bit Boys will never ask for a seed phrase. Check the address you typed, and prefer the official links on this site.
body.learn.wallets.353: A wallet here is software, or a hardware device, that holds keys and shows the addresses those keys control. This site will never ask you for a seed phrase. [Chapter 7, who holds the keys](/learn/custody), is the difference between an exchange login and that wallet.
body.learn.wallets.355: [Coinbase Wallet](https://wallet.coinbase.com/) is the self-custody wallet. It is separate from the Coinbase exchange in chapter 5. Assets in the exchange account are not the same record as assets in Coinbase Wallet until you withdraw.
body.learn.wallets.357: [MetaMask](https://metamask.io/) is a self-custody wallet used across EVM chains. Adding BNB Chain, a layer 2, or PulseChain is a network setting in the wallet. The same address can exist on each of those chains, and the balances are still per chain.
body.learn.wallets.359: [Internet Money](https://internetmoney.io/) describes its wallet as non-custodial and open source, for Bitcoin, Ethereum, and EVM chains, and says it collects no data.
body.learn.wallets.361: ZKX Wallet comes from Liberty Swap. It is a self-custodial browser extension, and a web app that can be installed as a progressive web app (PWA). It supports PulseChain and other EVM chains. It includes Railgun public and private modes, and it can swap and bridge inside the wallet.
body.learn.wallets.362: Blind Bit Boys works with that team so ZKX can be used with JAWS or NVDA. That work is underway. This page does not claim the wallet is already perfect.
body.learn.wallets.365: [ZKX Web3 Wallet on the Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/zkx-web3-wallet/fibfaangghabdbndamiaceoahiajfgck), offered by LibertySwap Developer
body.learn.yield.366: A swap pays the pool. Providing liquidity is how a person becomes part of that pool. A farm is often a second contract that pays an extra token for staying deposited. None of this is a rate you should expect to keep.
body.learn.yield.368: On an EVM chain, the common pool holds two tokens. You deposit both, in the proportion the pool asks for, and you receive a claim on a share of the trading fees. The same shape shows up on Ethereum, BNB Chain, Polygon, PulseChain, and other EVM networks. The contract addresses are not the same just because the tickers match. [Uniswap docs](https://docs.uniswap.org/) describe the pattern. The docs address currently stays on uniswap.org.
body.learn.yield.369: Where a Solana protocol offers a farm, it is the same idea on Solana’s programs: deposit, receive a share of fees or an extra token, and accept the risks below. Not every Solana token has a farm.
body.learn.yield.371: Impermanent loss is the gap between holding the two tokens in the pool and simply holding them in a wallet. If one token’s price moves far from the other, the pool rebalances by selling the one that rose and holding more of the one that fell. Fees can offset that gap. They do not have to. The name “impermanent” is hopeful. If you withdraw after the move, the gap is permanent.
body.learn.yield.373: The pool is a program. A bug, an upgrade key, or a function that lets the deployer withdraw the reserves can empty it. Chapter 3 names those failure modes. A fake site copies the exchange name and asks for an approval. Bookmark [the PulseX app](https://app.pulsex.com/) and [the Uniswap app](https://app.uniswap.org/) rather than following a search result.

body.page.instructions.411: Type a name, symbol, or contract address.
body.page.instructions.413: Results are headings under the heading Results. Activate a heading to open that token or pair.
body.page.instructions.414: The default page is Overview: name, ticker, price, liquidity, volume, the contract address, and the pair address.
body.page.instructions.415: Use the Paired Tokens tab for pools.
body.page.instructions.416: Use the Technical Analysis tab for charts.
body.page.instructions.417: Verified, boost verified, sort, and limit appear only when the data source is Moralis. They are inside an Advanced disclosure.
body.page.instructions.418: Overview and the Technical Analysis tab are unchanged: Overview is still the default token or pair page, and Technical Analysis is still a tab on that page.
body.page.instructions.420: The chart is a tab on a token page or a pair page. It is not a separate address. This page does not play sound.
body.page.instructions.421: From a token or pair page, open the Technical Analysis tab.
body.page.instructions.422: Data source is Gecko Terminal or Moralis, the same choice as Search. Currency is a separate labeled combo box.
body.page.instructions.423: Chart type is Candlestick or Line. Those are radio buttons.
body.page.instructions.424: Candle size is the width of each bar. Some sizes are disabled when that source cannot serve them. The option text says which source is missing.
body.page.instructions.425: Show last is how much history to load.
body.page.instructions.426: Date range uses the native Start date and time and End date and time fields. After you change them, press Generate Chart. Zooming inside the Highcharts chart is not the same as downloading a new range.
body.page.instructions.427: Indicators are checkboxes. Overlays sit on the price. Oscillators sit below it. Each checked indicator can have its own instrument.
body.page.instructions.428: Sonification starts with Price instrument. Order is Sequential or Simultaneous. Play all plays the chart. Play price only plays the price. Stop ends the sound.
body.page.instructions.429: The chart’s hamburger control is named Chart menu. It includes print, image downloads, and Download CSV.
body.page.instructions.431: Empty chart: try Gecko Terminal, a candle size that source can serve, and a shorter Show last.
body.page.instructions.432: Dates ignored: press Generate Chart after changing Start date and time or End date and time.
body.page.instructions.433: No sound: press Play all, check the system volume, and try another Price instrument.
